purpose: Additive Nigerian evidence from a fresh 2024-2026 review. Domain and sector evidence supplies context; role-pattern evidence is reserved for the role families directly supported by the cited source scope.

policy.nigeria: Use Nigerian government, regulator, professional-body, occupational-standard and explicitly Nigerian sector evidence for local context.
policy.scope: A domain or sector source does not establish that every role, tool, certificate or vacancy in that domain is Nigerian-specific.
policy.market: A vacancy or programme is a time-bound signal, not a universal requirement or demand ranking.
policy.licensing: Only a regulator, statute or explicit practice rule can support a licence or registration gate.

sources.name: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare hospital-services policy resources
sources.scope: Nigerian health-facility, laboratory quality, biosafety, patient-safety, eye-health and oxygen-care guidance
findings: The ministry lists a 2024 guideline on integration of medical laboratory services, a 2025 guideline on medical-laboratory quality management, and a 2026 guideline on laboratory biosafety and biosecurity.
The same policy resource lists patient-safety and care-quality guidance and an eye-health strategic plan for 2024-2028.
sources.limitations: These are system and practice guidance documents; they do not by themselves establish an individual licence or a vacancy for every health occupation.

sources.name: Federal Ministry of Health State of Health of the Nation Report 2024
sources.scope: Nigerian health-system workforce and service-delivery context reported for 2024
findings: The report describes Nigeria's primary, secondary and tertiary health-delivery levels and discusses doctors, dentists, mental-health and rehabilitation professionals in the national health system.
sources.limitations: The report is sector context, not a role-by-role vacancy census or universal competency specification.

sources.name: NBTE National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications brochure, January 2026 edition
sources.scope: Nigerian occupational and skills pathways across agriculture, animal husbandry, engineering, construction, ICT, fashion, hospitality, health and safety
findings: The brochure lists Nigerian NOS/NSQ pathways including aquaculture, crop production, animal husbandry, industrial automation, solar photovoltaic systems, welding and fabrication, garment making, food and beverage service, artificial intelligence, backend web development, cloud security engineering and other trades.
sources.limitations: A listed NOS/NSQ is evidence that a Nigerian training standard exists; it is not proof that every employer requires it or that every canonical role maps one-to-one to the trade title.

sources.name: Nigerian Film Corporation creative-media National Occupational Standards workshop
sources.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
sources.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

sources.name: Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission creative-economy sector map
sources.scope: Film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming, XR, arts and cultural tourism in Nigeria
findings: The NIPC sector page identifies film, music, fashion, live entertainment, digital content, animation, gaming and XR among Nigeria's creative-economy activities.
sources.limitations: Sector mapping shows an established Nigerian sector context; it does not establish role-level hiring volume or a required tool stack.

sources.name: Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy and Microsoft 3MTT workforce programme
sources.scope: Nigerian digital-skills pathways in AI, cybersecurity, data science and software development
findings: The ministry described 3MTT pathways for AI, cybersecurity, data science and software development and a Microsoft-backed AI skilling programme targeting Nigerian learners.
sources.limitations: A government skilling programme is ecosystem and pathway evidence, not proof that every Nigerian employer requires the programme or its tools.

sources.name: Office of the Head of the Civil Service ICT scheme-of-service circular
sources.scope: Federal Nigerian public-service ICT role classification and professional benchmark context
findings: The 2026 circular reports review and harmonisation of federal ICT schemes of service and describes professional benchmarks involving COREN for computer engineers and CPN registration for other IT specialists in the specified public-service progression context.
sources.limitations: The circular applies to the stated public-service scheme and must not be rendered as a blanket private-sector licence requirement.

sources.name: Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security National Agricultural Growth Strategy 2.0
sources.scope: Nigerian agriculture, food security, agribusiness, crop and livestock production and agricultural technology context
findings: The strategy document describes agriculture's Nigerian economic and food-security role and references the National Agricultural Technology and Innovation Policy 2022-2027.
sources.limitations: A national strategy establishes sector context and priorities, not a role-specific certification or employer requirement.

sources.name: Standards Organisation of Nigeria food and agriculture technical committees
sources.scope: Nigerian food, agriculture, animal-feed and veterinary-drug-residue standardisation
findings: SON lists technical committees covering animal feeds and veterinary-drug residues and antimicrobial resistance in food among Nigerian food and agriculture standards work.
sources.limitations: Technical-committee scope supports standards context; it is not by itself an individual certification or demand signal.

sources.name: Nigeria Customs Service Authorised Economic Operator programme
sources.scope: Nigerian importers, exporters, customs brokers, freight forwarders, transport and logistics operators
findings: The AEO material describes compliance, record management, customs knowledge, risk education, secure information exchange and supply-chain security for participating trade operators; the 2025 newsletter references the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023 legal basis and ISO 28001 for the security tier.
sources.limitations: AEO is an organisation/operator programme and does not make every listed control a personal certificate for every logistics or customs role.

sources.name: Construction and Labour Market Information System Nigerian construction National Occupational Standards
sources.scope: Nigerian construction trades including electrical, carpentry and joinery, masonry, painting, plumbing and tiling
findings: C-LMIS provides Nigerian construction National Occupational Standards across building trades, including electrical, carpentry and joinery, masonry, painting and decorating, plumbing and tiling.
sources.limitations: The standards support construction-trade skills and pathways; they do not establish a licence for every worker or a universal requirement for construction managers and engineers.

sources.name: Standards Organisation of Nigeria building and construction conference
sources.scope: Nigerian building construction standards, structural integrity, materials, risk management and sustainable development
findings: SON reported a 2024 national conference emphasizing standards practice, structural integrity, sustainable materials and risk management in Nigeria's building and construction industry.
sources.limitations: Conference and standards context does not assign one tool or credential to every construction role.

sources.name: Federal Government Nigerian welding, fabrication, foundry and instrumentation bootcamp
sources.scope: Nigerian youth technical training in welding, fabrication, foundry, metallurgy, instrumentation, control and mechanical maintenance
findings: The Federal Government reported training 535 Nigerian youths in welding and fabrication and related metals, instrumentation, control and mechanical-maintenance areas.
sources.limitations: The bootcamp is a skills-development signal and not a universal certificate or evidence that every metal-trade role is currently hiring.

sources.name: Federal Government social-work professionalisation and standards context
sources.scope: Nigerian social-work practice, professionalisation, standards and capacity-building context
findings: The Federal Government described work to strengthen social-work practice in Nigeria, including professionalisation and standards challenges under the Social Work Practitioners Act 2022 context.
sources.limitations: The article supports Nigerian practice context but does not establish one compulsory credential for every care, counselling or social-service role.

sources.name: Quantity Surveyors Registration Board of Nigeria 2024 newsletter
sources.scope: Nigerian quantity-surveying practice and professional registration context
findings: The QSRBN newsletter supplies Nigerian quantity-surveying professional-body context and practice material.
sources.limitations: The newsletter supports professional context; specific registration gates must be shown only where the applicable rule is explicit.

sources.name: NBTE Operational Guidelines for Sector Skills Councils
sources.scope: Nigerian sector-skills governance and occupational-standard development across ICT, engineering, transport/logistics and other sectors
findings: The guidelines describe sector-skills-council structures used to coordinate occupational standards, industry participation and skills development in Nigeria.
sources.limitations: The guidelines support skills-governance context and do not establish a credential or demand signal for an individual role.

sources.name: Nigeria Procurement Certification Programme
sources.scope: Nigerian public and private procurement practitioners
findings: The programme describes four Nigerian procurement-certification tiers and skills including communication, teamwork, time management, deadlines, ethics and risk management, with prerequisites varying by tier.
sources.limitations: The pathway is for procurement practice and does not apply to every purchasing, logistics, project or administrative role.

sources.name: Project Managers Development Association of Nigeria
sources.scope: Nigerian project-management professional development and IPMA-aligned certification levels
findings: PMDAN identifies itself as Nigeria's IPMA member association, describes four certification levels and publishes project-execution and project-management learning activities.
sources.limitations: Professional-body certification is a pathway, not a universal employer requirement for every project-support or coordination role.

sources.name: National Institute of Marketing of Nigeria
sources.scope: Nigerian marketing professional standards, training, certification and continuing development
findings: NIMN describes itself as the chartered regulatory body for marketing professionals in Nigeria and identifies training, certification, professional standards and ethics as part of its mandate.
sources.limitations: The source supports marketing-profession context; it does not establish a required certification for every marketing, sales, communications or brand role.

sources.name: Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority radiation-safety training for mining
sources.scope: Nigerian solid-mineral mining and processing radiation-safety roles and adjacent technical occupations
findings: NNRA announced a 2026 national course for current or prospective Radiation Safety Officers in mining and mineral processing, covering NORM/TE-NORM, monitoring, dose assessment, radiation protection, handling, transport, waste management and regulatory compliance.
sources.limitations: This is a specialised radiation-safety pathway and does not apply to every mining or geology role.

sources.name: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria practice and registration framework
sources.scope: Nigerian medicine, dentistry and alternative-medicine practice regulation, provisional registration and housemanship context
findings: MDCN describes its mandate to regulate medicine, dentistry and alternative medicine and provides provisional-registration, housemanship and practitioner-verification services.
sources.limitations: MDCN requirements apply to the regulated professions within its mandate, not to every health, biomedical or administrative role.

sources.name: COREN 2026 engineering regulation and public-safety reforms
sources.scope: Nigerian engineering practice, registration, public safety, project monitoring and anti-quackery context
findings: COREN's 2026 reforms emphasise qualified and registered practitioners, public safety, project monitoring and enforcement against unqualified engineering practice.
sources.limitations: The source supports regulated-engineering context; it is not a personal registration requirement for every technician or non-engineering role in an engineering organisation.

sources.name: COREN National Clean Energy Skills Certification Scheme
sources.scope: Nigerian renewable-energy and energy-efficiency skills and certification
findings: COREN describes itself as the national certification body for clean-energy skills and reports revalidation of competency standards in July 2024 and a 2025 partnership with NEMSA for renewable-energy and energy-efficiency certification.
sources.limitations: This supports clean-energy skills certification context; it is not a universal licence for every energy or electrical role.

sources.name: NEMSA and REAN renewable-energy safety and standards partnership
sources.scope: Nigerian renewable-energy installation safety, standardisation and quality assurance
findings: NEMSA reported collaboration with the Renewable Energy Association of Nigeria to strengthen safety, standardisation and quality assurance and stated that installations should be carried out by certified professionals under national requirements.
sources.limitations: The statement concerns renewable-energy installations and does not impose one certificate on every energy-adjacent role.

sources.name: NESREA national environmental-regulation review
sources.scope: Nigerian chemicals, waste, energy and environmental-management standards
findings: NESREA reported review of national environmental regulations covering chemicals and waste management and highlighted the role of industry, government, civil society and research in environmental management.
sources.limitations: Regulatory review supports environmental-practice context; it does not establish a certificate or a particular tool for every environmental role.

sources.name: NIMASA seafarer education, training, certification and medical-fitness standards
sources.scope: Nigerian seafarer education, assessment, certification, revalidation, endorsement and medical fitness
findings: NIMASA reported revised standards under Nigeria's 2025 STCW regulations, including education, training, assessment, examination, certification, revalidation, endorsement and medical-fitness requirements, with bridging courses for specified ND/HND holders.
sources.limitations: These standards apply to seafarer roles and do not apply to every maritime, port, logistics or naval-architecture occupation.

sources.name: Central Bank of Nigeria banking-sector recapitalisation programme
sources.scope: Nigerian banking-sector capital, licensing and regulatory context through March 2026
findings: CBN describes the 2024 banking recapitalisation programme, including minimum paid-in capital requirements by licence category and a compliance period ending March 31, 2026.
sources.limitations: This is bank and licence-level regulatory context, not a skill or personal certification requirement for every banking employee.

sources.name: ICAN professional syllabus 2026
sources.scope: Nigerian accountancy, audit, financial reporting, banking, insurance, tax and public-finance competency context
findings: The 2026 syllabus covers Nigerian financial-reporting and professional-accountancy topics including banking, insurance, taxation, financial reporting and relevant Nigerian legislation.
sources.limitations: A syllabus supports a professional pathway and competency map; it does not establish that every finance or banking role requires ICAN.

sources.name: Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria teacher standards and PQE
sources.scope: Nigerian teacher education, accreditation, registration, professional qualifying examination and competency assessment
findings: TRCN describes its responsibility for teacher-education standards, programme accreditation, qualification approval, professional registration and competency assessment; its 2026 updates include PQE results and school-accreditation policy implementation.
sources.limitations: TRCN applies to teaching practice within its mandate, not to every education, training, research or childcare role.

sources.name: Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission generation-licence requirements
sources.scope: Nigerian on-grid, off-grid and embedded electricity-generation facilities
findings: NERC describes generation licences and associated environmental-impact or effluent-management documentation for specified Nigerian generation facilities.
sources.limitations: This is a facility/operator licence context, not a personal licence for every energy worker.

sources.name: Nigeria Data Protection Commission legal-practice and compliance guidance
sources.scope: Nigerian legal, compliance, audit, privacy and data-protection practice
findings: NDPC guidance discusses accountability, data minimisation, confidentiality, records, audits and compliance returns for legal practices and organisations handling personal data; it also describes licensed Data Protection Compliance Organisations and relevant expertise areas.
sources.limitations: The source supports data-protection and compliance capability; it does not make every lawyer, compliance officer or IT worker a DPCO or data-protection specialist.

sources.name: Bureau of Public Service Reforms National Strategy for Public Service Reform
sources.scope: Nigerian civil-service administration, competency, performance, accountability and professionalisation
findings: The strategy describes a professional, results-oriented, competent, accountable and citizen-centred Nigerian public service, including merit-based recruitment, performance management, job evaluation and professionalisation of core cadres.
sources.limitations: A reform strategy supplies public-service capability context, not a universal qualification for every public or private-sector role.

sources.name: OHCSF Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis project
sources.scope: Nigerian federal civil-service skills identification, development and gap analysis
findings: The OHCSF PASGA portal describes a project to identify and develop the skills of Nigerian public servants and build a data-driven, globally competitive civil service.
sources.limitations: The portal is public-service skills context and does not establish a private-sector requirement or a single certification.

sources.name: TRCN safeguarding resources for Nigerian schools
sources.scope: Nigerian child protection, learner safety, violence-free schools and safeguarding practice
findings: TRCN provides resources on child protection, safety, security and violence-free schools and describes protocols and standards for protecting children and learners.
sources.limitations: Safeguarding resources support education and child-facing practice; they do not create one universal certificate for all social-service or childcare roles.

sources.name: Nigerian Notary Public Regulations and electronic notary register
sources.scope: Nigerian notarial practice, registration and digital-signature/seal context
findings: The 2026 notice and electronic notary information describe registration on the Electronic Notary Register and compliance with Nigerian notarial practice requirements.
sources.limitations: This is specific to notarial practice and does not apply to every legal, compliance or administrative role.

sources.name: NBRDA genetics, genomics and bioinformatics workshop
sources.scope: Nigerian molecular biology, genetics, genomics, bioinformatics and public research infrastructure
findings: NBRDA reported a practical workshop through its Genetics, Genomics and Bioinformatics Department and connected it to Nigeria BioGenome and national genomics/bioinformatics data infrastructure goals.
sources.limitations: The workshop supports Nigerian research and skills context; it does not establish broad private-sector demand or a universal certificate.

sources.name: University of Ibadan AFRIGENE genomics and computational-skills programme
sources.scope: Nigerian genomics, bioinformatics, computational biology, evolutionary biology and biodiversity research skills
findings: The University of Ibadan described AFRIGENE 2026 hands-on learning focused on computational tools and approaches for genomics, evolutionary biology and biodiversity conservation.
sources.limitations: University training is research and capacity-building evidence, not a role-specific vacancy or licence requirement.

sources.name: Esports Federation of Nigeria national esports programmes
sources.scope: Nigerian competitive gaming, schools and university esports, broadcasting, refereeing, tournament operations and team programmes
findings: The federation described a National Esports Championship, Team Nigeria programme, schools and university league, and training for referees, broadcasters and tournament officials.
sources.limitations: Federation programmes demonstrate ecosystem and role-family context; they do not establish national job volume or a mandatory credential.

sources.name: Nigerian XR and immersive-technology ecosystem signals
sources.scope: Lagos and Nigerian AR/VR/XR training, immersive media, education, healthcare and construction use cases
findings: Lagos XR ecosystem sources describe skills including 360 video, Unity, Unreal Engine, event planning and team leadership; local reporting also describes VR training and Nigerian immersive-technology education and emergency-services use cases.
sources.limitations: These are ecosystem and training signals, not evidence of a national vacancy count or universal tool requirement.

sources.name: NIPES 2025 Nigerian quantum-computing conference contribution
sources.scope: Nigerian research and conference interest in quantum-computing architectures and future technology
findings: The NIPES 2025 book of abstracts includes a contribution on advances in quantum computing and scalable error-corrected quantum processors.
sources.limitations: This establishes Nigerian research/conference interest, not a local quantum-computing job market, employer demand, or Nigerian professional certification.
